result_text:
All four broken default conventions now match their intended files. The new test passes (7 of 7), and the rest of the `codeanalyzer` suite was not run.

Changes in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`:

- **Generated HTML:** the pkgdown, Doxygen and meta-generator rules now use `(html|htm|xhtml)` instead of `(html|html|xhtml)`.
- **.NET docs XML:** the path pattern is `.*[.]xml` instead of `.*/[.]xml`.
- **`// Generated by` JavaScript:** the path pattern is `.*[.]js` instead of `.*/[.]js`.
- **Gradle JavaScript:** the build-and-deployment pattern is `.*[-]gradle[.]js` instead of `.*[.][-]gradle[.]js`.

The old `.*/[.]js` and `.*/[.]xml` patterns required the file name to be exactly `.js` or `.xml`. The new patterns match any file with that extension. Each rule still needs its content pattern, so hand-written `.htm`, `.js` and `.xml` files stay out of those scopes.

I added `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventionsTest.java`. It covers positive and negative cases for each fixed rule, plus the existing Doxygen `.html`, `.xhtml` meta-generator and `build.gradle` cases. The test run was `mvn -q -o -pl codeanalyzer test -Dtest=ScopingConventionsTest`. Nothing is committed.
